chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Khalid ibn Tahman, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
When you laugh loudly (guffaw), say when you finish: 'O Allah, do not detest me.'

key_terms.تَفْرُغُ: To finish or cease (from the act of laughing)
key_terms.لَا تَمْقُتْنِي: Do not detest me / Do not be displeased with me

ai.seo_question: What should one say after laughing loudly according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise supplication from Imam al-Baqir (AS), linking the physical act of loud laughter (qahqahah) to spiritual mindfulness. Scholars note that this dhikr serves as a corrective measure to prevent the heart from becoming heedless or arrogant during moments of uninhibited joy, ensuring that levity does not lead to spiritual negligence.
